facts.fact: Braves start Chris Sale (14-9, 2.16 ERA, 0.98 WHIP, 200 K); 2.08 ERA in four starts vs Philadelphia this season.
Phillies open with Jesus Luzardo (left shoulder inflammation, no start since Sept. 7, not built up), with rookie Andrew Painter following; they hope the pair covers 6-7 innings.
Luis Arraez (left ankle sprain) ruled out for Philadelphia; Braves' Lane Thomas (left intercostal strain) likely unavailable.
Phillies vs left-handed starters this season: .300 OBP, .680 OPS, 21-26 record; went 2-4 in their final two series.
Braves ML dipped from -206 to -194 and was bet back to -205; Braves run line drew 65.5% of tickets but 94.5% of handle.
Atlanta forecast: sunny, dry, low-to-mid 80s at first pitch.

games.judgment: Everything here is public and the market already has Atlanta at 64%. The piece I think is under-weighted is the Phillies' pitching: an opener coming off shoulder inflammation plus a rookie bulk arm, against Sale, who has owned this lineup, with Arraez out of an already weak lineup vs lefties. Big-money run-line action agrees. I nudge Atlanta up about 1 point and like the run line best, since a Braves win here is more likely to be comfortable than a one-run walk-off. Warm and dry doesn't change the total much.

estimates.rationale: Sale (2.08 ERA vs PHI) against a Phillies patchwork of an opener fresh off shoulder inflammation and a rookie. Philly hits lefties poorly (.680 OPS) and is without Arraez.
estimates.key_risk: Luzardo is sharp early and Painter gets through the middle innings; a one-run game is a coin flip in the late innings.

estimates.rationale: If Atlanta wins it is likely because Philly's bulk pitching leaks runs, which tends to produce margins of two or more. Heavy handle on this line points the same way.
estimates.key_risk: Home teams can't win by more than one in a walk-off; a tight 3-2 game kills it.

estimates.rationale: Sale suppresses runs, but the Phillies' bullpen-heavy plan is likely to allow some. Warm, dry day game. No strong view; staying at market.
estimates.key_risk: Sale goes seven and Philly's pen holds.

facts.fact: Both teams use bullpen games: Houston opens with AJ Blubaugh (5-3, 3.66 ERA; MLB-leading 96 relief innings); Chicago opens with Hagen Smith (1.29 ERA in 28 IP) followed by Erick Fedde (8-9, 3.83 ERA; 4.88 ERA on the road).
White Sox were 36-45 on the road (worst of any playoff team); Astros were 39-42 at home and have lost four straight home playoff games.
White Sox offense ranked fifth in runs and fifth in homers (211) but strikes out a lot; Colson Montgomery has 31 HR, a .197 average and a record 227 strikeouts.
Blubaugh held the White Sox scoreless over four innings in three regular-season appearances.

games.judgment: The line has moved hard toward Chicago (Houston opened -146, now -117 to -126). I don't have a specific fact that explains the move, so I respect it rather than fight it. Two bullpen games at an indoor park with a power-heavy White Sox lineup make me lean slightly over, but only slightly.

estimates.rationale: Houston has home field and a rested, deep bullpen plan, but the market has moved 5+ points toward Chicago without public news. Holding at the market.
estimates.key_risk: Chicago's power (211 HR) makes any bullpen game volatile.

estimates.rationale: Two bullpen games expose more middle relievers, and Fedde has a 4.88 road ERA. Indoor park, a power-heavy lineup on one side. Small lean over.
estimates.key_risk: Playoff bullpens are shortened to the best arms; Chicago strikes out a lot.

facts.fact: This is the 2026-27 NHL regular-season opener for both teams (0-0-0), 5 p.m. ET.
Projected goalies: Jacob Markstrom (FLA) and Brandon Bussi (CAR), both unconfirmed as of the morning.
Florida without Brad Marchand (August surgery, out about a month) and Jonah Gadjovich; Carolina without Seth Jarvis (shoulder, not before late October).

games.judgment: Injuries roughly offset (Marchand vs Jarvis). The line moved from Carolina -130 toward Florida (-117 to -125 now). Opening-night data is thin; no reason to deviate from market.

estimates.rationale: Offsetting injuries and unconfirmed goalies. Staying near the market's 53%.
estimates.key_risk: Goalie confirmation could flip this either way.

estimates.rationale: Two structured defensive teams, with both teams' top scoring wings (Marchand, Jarvis) missing. Market already leans under; I agree, no more.
estimates.key_risk: Opening-night special teams can be sloppy.

facts.fact: Regular-season opener at Scotiabank Arena, 7 p.m. ET.
Projected goalies: Sergei Bobrovsky (TOR, newly signed) vs Jakub Dobes (MTL), both unconfirmed.
Toronto's offseason additions include Bobrovsky and Gavin McKenna.

games.judgment: The books disagree: DraftKings prices Toronto at about 51.7% no-vig (-118), and it opened -115, while Polymarket is a coin flip. With the home opener and Bobrovsky over Dobes in goal, I side with DraftKings and think Polymarket's even-money Toronto price is a touch generous. Small edge, low confidence.

estimates.rationale: Toronto at home with Bobrovsky projected against Dobes. DraftKings has Toronto -118; Polymarket's +100 looks slightly stale.
estimates.key_risk: Goalies unconfirmed; rivalry openers are high-variance.

estimates.rationale: No strong view; the market leans under and I stay there.
estimates.key_risk: Both teams can score in bunches.

facts.fact: Yankees start Cam Schlittler (14-6, 1.95 ERA; 0.74 ERA and 27 K in 24 1/3 IP over four starts vs Boston).
Red Sox start LHP Payton Tolle (9-6, 3.03 ERA; 5-0, 2.66 ERA over his final 13 starts; 0.69 ERA in two starts vs New York).
Aaron Judge (right soleus strain, suffered Sept. 16) got a platelet-poor plasma injection Monday; Boone said the team is preparing as if Judge won't be available but has not ruled him out.
Entire series at Yankee Stadium, 8 p.m. ET first pitch.

games.judgment: Two starters who have dominated these exact lineups, and the best hitter on the field is likely out or limited. The Yankees line has come down from -142 (Polymarket -127), which fits Judge news being priced in. I don't have a side, but I think the under is the best number: 6.5 already, and the market still has the over at 47%. Low confidence because lineups aren't out yet.

estimates.rationale: Schlittler is the better starter, but Judge's likely absence offsets it and the market has adjusted. At market.
estimates.key_risk: Judge plays and is fully effective.

estimates.rationale: Schlittler (0.74 ERA vs BOS) and Tolle (0.69 ERA vs NYY) have both shut these lineups down, and Judge is likely out or limited. Two good bullpens behind them in a playoff game.
estimates.key_risk: A short start by the rookie Tolle, or Judge playing, pushes this over quickly.

facts.fact: Regular-season opener at TD Garden, 8 p.m. ET.
Jeremy Swayman starts for Boston (coach Marco Sturm: 'definitely our guy'); Igor Shesterkin projected for New York (1.81 GAA, .917 in two preseason starts).

games.judgment: This line has swung hard, from Boston -142 at open to a coin flip. That is a big move and I have no fact to fight it, so I stay at 50%. Two elite goalies make me reluctant to take the over at a juiced 5.5.

estimates.rationale: The market moved from Boston -142 to pick'em; respecting it. No edge either way.
Shesterkin vs Swayman argues for fewer goals, so I shade the over slightly below the market's 54%.
estimates.key_risk: Opening-night rust from the skaters in front of them.

facts.fact: Padres start Michael King (12-10, 3.21 ERA; 2.74 ERA, 1.12 WHIP, .212 opponent average in 15 home starts).
Cubs start LHP Matthew Boyd (10-5, 3.91 ERA, 96 K and 39 BB in 126 2/3 IP).

Padres bullpen: Mason Miller closes, Adrian Morejon sets up; Jeremiah Estrada unavailable (shoulder impingement). Cubs have no set closer. Cubs' Kevin Gausman is unavailable (left shoulder soreness); Alex Bregman is back from facial fractures.

games.judgment: King at home has been excellent and the Padres have the clearer late-inning bullpen (Miller/Morejon vs a committee). I shade San Diego up about a point. The total has come down from 7.5 to 7, and a night game at Petco with King starting fits an under lean.

estimates.rationale: King's home numbers (2.74 ERA) and the stronger back-end bullpen give San Diego a small edge beyond the price.
estimates.key_risk: Boyd has been solid, and Chicago's lineup has power throughout.

estimates.rationale: Pitcher-friendly park at night, King at home, and the total already dropping from 7.5. Probability excludes a push on 7.
estimates.key_risk: Two good offenses; one big inning goes over.

facts.fact: Regular-season opener at Rogers Place; new Oilers coach Mike Babcock.
Tristan Jarry is confirmed to start for Edmonton; he posted a 3.86 GAA and .857 save percentage last season. Kevin Lankinen projected for Vancouver.

games.judgment: 72% is a big number for an NHL regular-season game. Edmonton is starting a goalie who was among the league's worst last season, and money has pushed Vancouver out from +215 to +257. I think the market is slightly too high on Edmonton; I take a small amount of value on Vancouver. Low confidence.

estimates.rationale: Jarry (.857 last season) is a real weakness behind a heavy favorite, and NHL underdogs at +250 win more often than bettors expect. Small value on Vancouver.
estimates.key_risk: McDavid and Draisaitl can win any game on their own.

estimates.rationale: A weak Edmonton goalie in front of an elite offense. Slight over lean, at market.
estimates.key_risk: Babcock's defensive system tightens things up.

facts.fact: Regular-season opener in Las Vegas; Golden Knights' 10th season.
Spencer Knight likely starts for Chicago (Arvid Soderblom later on the road trip). Carter Hart is Vegas's projected starter (unconfirmed).
Chicago's opening lines are young (Moore-Kantserov-Kane; Bertuzzi-Frondell-Mangiapane; Donato-Nazar-Lardis).

games.judgment: Vegas is deep and at home against a rebuilding team. The price (about 71%) reflects that. No specific news to move it.

estimates.rationale: Deeper Vegas roster at home against a young Chicago lineup. At market.
estimates.key_risk: Spencer Knight can steal a game.

estimates.rationale: No edge; staying near the market's 55%.
